$comment: The publication allowlist. The app build vendors EXACTLY what is listed here.
A skill present in skills/ but absent from this file is not shipped — so adding a
directory is not enough to publish it. Changing this file is the decision to publish,
and it is reviewable on its own in a pull request.
Keep 'why' populated. Six months from now it is the only record of the intent.

publish.why: Routes questions to the right warehouse source and documents the table/column landscape. Without it the agent has no map of the warehouse.

The app exposes a create_sigma_workbook tool but nothing told the model what a valid spec looks like, so any dashboard request produced an invented shape. Upstream sigma-authoring plugin v1.12.2 by Thomas Wells (MIT), stripped of scripts/ (Ruby+shell the sandbox cannot run) and generated/ (copies for other AI tools), plus SENTA-ADDENDUM.md for local findings.

Every deck and document the app produces should be board-ready without reformatting. Reverse-engineered by measuring a deck the executive team accepted (APP_Landscape_Platform_Review), then moved onto the brand palette with the contrast arithmetic done: teal #005f7f replaces the navy as the structural colour because theme.css already designates it as chrome, and brand blue #0071ce is data-only since it measures 4.36:1 on the card surface and fails the 4.5 floor. Carries the grid, type scale, table style, editorial rules and the logo asset.

$notes.tiers: Which app tiers receive the skill. 'consumer' = the ~139 viewer seats, 'pro' = the ~13 analyst seats.
$notes.owner: Who reviews changes to it. Matches CODEOWNERS.
recipes: Ids from recipes/, without the .json. Same gate as skills: a file present in that
directory but absent from this list is not shipped. See recipes/README.md.
A recipe bypasses the app's methodology gate — the review happened here instead, in
the pull request — so the build refuses to publish one without a named approvedBy.
